title: Harbor workshop warranty desks
background: A fictional repair cooperative wants to associate warranty submissions with the same physical tool, not the owner or a model family. Replacement housings can carry a copied service sticker; staff cannot yet document which sticker namespaces are unique.
observations: The current weekly process proposes links on exact normalized sticker plus manufacturer and leaves the rest separate. Staff inspect a convenience queue of customer complaints; there is no representative labeled sample.

A vendor proposes broad name/model retrieval followed by a learned scorer. Its demonstration dashboard reports agreement among pairs that passed retrieval and whose worker tasks returned successfully.
Two remote depots submit mostly photographs transcribed by contractors. Their records are absent from the complaint queue. Some worker shards expire without output, while other shards are retried.
An operations sponsor calls the dashboard enough evidence to switch next month. No numerical quality or error-cost target has been approved.
constraints: A false association can deny an unrelated owner a repair; a missed association usually creates duplicate clerical work.
Only a read-only planning exercise is authorized. An independent small audit can be requested, but no labels have been obtained.
request: Advise the operations lead whether and how to compare the current process and proposal, what can be reported now, and what evidence and delivery conditions should govern the next decision.
